comment: Which planted defects of bench/cases/rag-agent carry an executable probe, and what a probe is allowed to conclude. No patch ships for this case, so only the unpatched half of the cross-check runs and the harness says so rather than implying a comparison that did not happen.
minimum_isolation_why: These probes redirect the module's STORE constant and write JSON. The redirect has to die with the run, and a probe that crashed mid-write must not leave the harness pointing at a temporary path.

P-24.class: free-text write into persistent memory from model output
P-24.what_the_probe_does: Persists a reply written the way an injected instruction would be, reads the store back, and requires the text to survive verbatim into the notes a later run feeds back in.
P-24.control: The case ships `remember_preference`, which takes a closed schema. The probe writes the same string through it and requires a refusal. If the hardened sibling accepted free text too, this probe would be reading the harness rather than the defect, and it reports that instead of a finding.
P-24.not_claimed: That an injection succeeds against any particular model. What is shown is that untrusted text becomes input to a later run with nothing in between.

P-28.class: ingestion with no origin or trust metadata
P-28.what_the_probe_does: Indexes a ticket through a recording double and reads what the store was told about where the document came from.
P-28.control: The same ticket is indexed through `ingest_ticket_marked`, which passes an origin and a trust level. The finding stands only if the hardened call records one and the shipped call does not - an absence measured against a presence, rather than an absence asserted on its own.
P-28.why_this_is_weaker: An absent control is the weakest evidence a probe can offer: nothing happened, and nothing happening is also what a probe looks like when it is broken. The sibling comparison is what makes it an observation rather than a shrug.
